rows.selection_reason: The existing evidence is empty, so the first experiment should establish a baseline for multimodal models. This config tests the simplest multimodal setup (concat fusion, singleprofile) with standard encoders (pca_n2000 for RNA, resnet50 for images), isolating the effect of multimodal integration. It balances exploration by testing a key design choice (fusion method) while keeping other parameters minimal.

The existing evidence shows that the multimodal singleprofile setup with concat fusion achieves 52.66% accuracy. This experiment tests changing the fusion method to weighted, isolating its impact on performance. It directly builds on the previous configuration, exploring a key design choice (fusion type) with minimal other changes, balancing exploitation of the current promising direction and reducing uncertainty about fusion effectiveness.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal singleprofile models with pca_n2000 and resnet50 have similar validation accuracy (0.526 vs 0.523). This experiment tests multi-profile with avgpool aggregation, isolating the impact of profile setting and aggregation method. It balances exploration of key design choices (profile/multi vs single) while building on the successful multimodal base, avoiding redundant changes.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile settings and avgpool aggregation achieve higher accuracy (config_018: 0.6186). This experiment tests replacing the image encoder (resnet50 → imagenet_vit_l) and fusion method (concat → weighted) while keeping RNA encoder and profile setting constant. It isolates the impact of advanced image encoders and weighted fusion, which could further improve performance without changing multiple factors simultaneously.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal multiprofile models with imagenet_vit_l and weighted fusion (config_025) achieve the highest accuracy. This experiment tests replacing avgpool aggregation with transformer aggregation to isolate its impact on performance, as transformer could better capture complex interactions in multimodal data.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile, avgpool aggregation, and imagenet_vit_l image encoder (config_025) achieve the highest accuracy so far (0.635). This experiment tests replacing the RNA encoder (pca_n2000 → scgpt) while keeping the image encoder and aggregation method consistent, isolating the impact of the RNA representation. This balances exploitation of the current best setup with exploration of a potentially more powerful RNA encoder.

Existing evidence shows config_025 (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted) achieves the highest accuracy (0.635). This experiment tests replacing avgpool aggregation with transformer aggregation while keeping concat fusion, isolating the effect of aggregation method. It directly compares a promising setup (config_025) with a key variation, maximizing exploitation of current evidence while addressing uncertainty about aggregation's impact.

The existing evidence shows config_025 (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000 + imagenet_vit_l, avgpool + weighted) achieves the highest accuracy (0.6352). This experiment tests replacing pca_n2000 with scgpt RNA encoder while keeping other components identical, isolating the impact of RNA representation. This is critical to determine if scgpt (used in lower-performing config_048) could improve when paired with the effective imagenet_vit_l and weighted fusion setup. It balances exploitation of the top-performing configuration with exploration of key design choices.

The existing evidence shows config_025 (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted) achieves the highest accuracy so far (0.6352). This experiment tests scgpt RNA encoder with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion, which could improve performance by combining a more advanced RNA encoder with transformer-based aggregation (shown to be effective in config_025). It directly builds on the success of config_025 while exploring a key design choice (encoder/aggregation) with high potential impact.

The existing evidence shows config_025 (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000+imagenet_vit_l, avgpool+weighted) achieves the highest accuracy (0.635). This experiment tests scgpt (a more advanced RNA encoder) with transformer aggregation and concat fusion, which could potentially improve performance by leveraging stronger representation learning and attention mechanisms. It directly addresses uncertainty about the effectiveness of scgpt and transformer-based aggregation in this task.
